policy_title: Reform the planning system for sustainable development and protect green spaces
stated: Transform the planning system to reduce environmental impact, require small developments across areas, protect the Green Belt, ensure new homes meet Passivhaus or equivalent standards with solar panels and heat pumps, and ensure new developments are supported by infrastructure and discourage car dependency.

source.quote: We will transform the planning system to reduce the environmental impact of new construction and to require local authorities to spread small developments across their areas, where appropriate, rather than building huge new estates. Greens are also committed to protecting the Green Belt and ensuring everybody has easy access to a green space. Elected Greens will campaign to change building regulations so all new homes meet Passivhaus or equivalent standards and to require house builders to include solar panels and low carbon heating systems such as heat pumps for all new homes. New developments need to ensure that residents are not car dependent.

bearing_set.reason: Passivhaus/solar/heat-pump mandates, car-dependency reduction, and explicit environmental-impact requirements directly target emissions trajectories and environmental quality — the primary purpose of the policy.

Green Belt protection constrains developable land supply while Passivhaus and renewable-energy requirements raise build costs, both materially affecting housing affordability and net supply — core O1 indicators.

Passivhaus standards plus mandatory solar panels and heat pumps would substantially reduce energy bills for occupants of new homes, a non-negligible effect on the energy-cost component of cost of living.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O6 is the primary intended benefit (environment/climate); O1 captures the well-documented supply/cost tradeoff (stricter standards + Green Belt protection raise costs and limit land); O2 captures the energy-bill relief for occupants of high-efficiency new homes. Effects on O13 (economic mobility via infrastructure/car-dependency) and O14 (distributional access to high-spec housing) are real but secondary to these three and adequately subsumed within them at this stage.
